text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today after climbing sharply yesterday on Middle East tensions. The decline came as oil prices steadied rather than continued climbing—U.S. crude sits at $91.48, down from yesterday's spike driven by Iran's missile strikes on Kuwait and drone attacks. The stock had jumped 0.7% just the day before on the back of those geopolitical risks pushing prices higher, but today's pullback suggests traders are taking profits now that the immediate shock has worn off.

The broader picture shows oil prices still up significantly this week despite today's dip, with U.S. crude gaining over 9% from the start of the week's hostilities. ConocoPhillips remains up 0.6% over the past two weeks, reflecting how energy companies benefit when geopolitical risk pushes crude higher—but individual days' moves hinge on whether those risks are still escalating or stabilizing.
